newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks capital transfer in plane production.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks capital transfer in plane production.

text.p: Turkey's plans for joint aircraft production with McDonnell Douglas Corp include a request for a capital transfer, an adviser to the prime minister said on Friday.
McDonnell Douglas has proposed the joint manufacture of MD-90 aircraft in Turkey, the chief prime ministry adviser Sedat Celikdogan told Reuters.
"The company brought the proposal to make the MD-90 in Turkey. They proposed an 80 percent local contribution. We want them to bring capital for the manufacture of this aircraft," Celikdogan said.
"We do not want technology transfer, we want capital transfer. We told them that," he said.
Turkey has finished the assessment of aircraft production proposals made by McDonnell Douglas, Boeing Co and Airbus Industrie.
Celikdogan said Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was expected to give the final decision in the coming days on which of the proposals would be accepted.
Turkey has sought the bids to meet the demand of national carrier Turkish Airlines for 54 passenger aircraft.

Turkish officials say the three companies have accepted Turkey's proposal that the aircraft be produced under a 50 percent offset agreement. Under such an agreement, 50 percent of the sum paid for the aircraft is awarded to domestic industry in the form of contracts.

The planned agreement envisages the manufacture of 34 planes in a first batch, followed by a second batch of 20 aircraft, the officials said. They said deliveries could begin next year if orders are presented this year.
